description: Create an Adaptive LMS (Least Mean Squares) filter in Verilog. The LMS filter will update its weights based on the incoming data samples and the desired output. The filter should take an input signal, a desired signal, and produce an output signal based on the current weights. The weights should be updated at each clock cycle based on the LMS algorithm. The filter will have a tap length of 4.
code:
module adaptive_lms_filter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire signed [15:0] x,         // input signal
    input wire signed [15:0] d,         // desired signal
    output reg signed [15:0] y          // output signal
);

    parameter N = 4;                    // number of taps
    parameter mu = 16'h0001;            // step size for weight adjustment

    reg signed [15:0] w [0:N-1];        // weights
    reg signed [15:0] x_delay [0:N-1];  // delayed input signals

    integer i;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            // Reset weights and delayed inputs
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= 16'h0000;          // Initialize weights to zero
                x_delay[i] <= 16'h0000;    // Initialize delays to zero
            end
            y <= 16'h0000;                  // Reset output
        end else begin
            // Shift input samples
            for (i = N-1; i > 0; i = i - 1) begin
                x_delay[i] <= x_delay[i-1];
            end
            x_delay[0] <= x;                // New input sample

            // Calculate output
            y <= 16'h0000;                  // Initialize output
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                y <= y + w[i] * x_delay[i]; // Multiply and sum
            end

            // Update weights
            for (i = 0; i < N; i = i + 1) begin
                w[i] <= w[i] + (mu * (d - y) * x_delay[i]) >>> 8; // LMS weight update
            end
        end
    end
endmodule

    input [31:0] x1, 
    input [31:0] y1, 
    input [31:0] x2, 
    input [31:0] y2, 
    input start,
    output reg [31:0] x3,
    output reg [31:0] y3,
    output reg done
);

        // Simplified ECC point addition for demonstration

            // Regular point addition, resulting in a new point
            x3 = (x1 + x2) % 32'hFFFFFFFF; // Dummy addition
            y3 = (y1 + y2) % 32'hFFFFFFFF; // Dummy addition
        end
        done = 1;
    end
endmodule

Design a JK flip-flop with asynchronous reset and preset inputs. The flip-flop should have inputs J, K, Clock, Reset, and Preset, and outputs Q and Qn. The behavior of the flip-flop should be defined as follows:
- On the rising edge of the Clock:
  - If Reset is high, Q should be reset to 0.
  - If Preset is high, Q should be set to 1.
  - If J and K are both 0, Q remains unchanged.
  - If J is 1 and K is 0, Q is set to 1.
  - If J is 0 and K is 1, Q is set to 0.
  - If J and K are both 1, Q toggles.
code:
module JK_flip_flop (
    input wire J,
    input wire K,
    input wire Clock,
    input wire Reset,
    input wire Preset,
    output reg Q,
    output wire Qn
);
    assign Qn = ~Q;

    always @(posedge Clock or posedge Reset or posedge Preset) begin
        if (Reset) begin
            Q <= 0;
        end else if (Preset) begin
            Q <= 1;
        end else begin
            case ({J, K})
                2'b00: Q <= Q;          // No Change
                2'b01: Q <= 0;          // Reset
                2'b10: Q <= 1;          // Set
                2'b11: Q <= ~Q;         // Toggle
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

    input wire serial_in,
    output reg [3:0] parallel_out

endmodule

    parameter RECEIVING = 2'b11;

            sender_state <= IDLE;
            receiver_state <= IDLE;

            case (sender_state)
                IDLE: begin

                        sender_state <= SENDING;

                        sender_state <= IDLE; // Frame sent and acknowledged

    input start,

    input MISO,
    output reg SCLK,
    output reg CS
);

    reg [7:0] shift_reg;

            state <= 0;
            MOSI <= 0;
            SCLK <= 0;
            CS <= 1; // Chip select inactive
            bit_count <= 0;
            shift_reg <= 0;
        end else begin

                    CS <= 1;
                    if (start) begin
                        CS <= 0; // Activate chip select
                        shift_reg <= data_in;
                        bit_count <= 0;
                        state <= 1; // go to start state
                    end

                1: begin // start

                    state <= 2; // go to transmit state

                        SCLK <= 1; // Clock high

                        state <= 4; // go to done state
                    end

                3: begin // receive

                        // Receiving data from MISO

                        bit_count <= bit_count + 1;
                        state <= 2; // back to transmit
                    end else begin
                        state <= 4; // go to done
                    end
                end
                4: begin // done
                    CS <= 1; // Deactivate chip select
                    state <= 0; // back to idle
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
